reasoning:
The user wants a hard, concrete treatment of "consensus-illusion detection": separating true agreement from N correlated hallucinations, in a "verkle chain / provenance gate" context. They want measured signals and a closed-form decision rule. This is a technical systems/ML/verification problem. Let me think about what this actually means and build the real machinery.

Context interpretation: We have N independent(?) verifiers/models producing outputs (e.g., answers, attestations, proofs). They agree — but agreement may be genuine (independent convergence on truth) or an illusion (correlated hallucination: shared training data, shared prompt, shared tool failure, shared upstream source, copy-paste, same seed, same retrieval corpus poisoning). The "verkle chain / provenance gate" suggests: each output carries provenance metadata hashed into a Verkle tree; the gate admits/rejects consensus based on measured signals computed over the provenance tree plus output-level signals.

Goal: a decision rule D(observed signals) → {true-consensus, correlated-hallucination}, with closed form, calibrated thresholds, measurable quantities.

Let me structure this rigorously.

## 1. Formalize the generative model

Two hypotheses:

- H_T (true consensus): each agent i produces answer y_i = f*(x) + ε_i, where ε_i are conditionally independent given x (or at least weakly dependent), with error rate p_i. Agreement arises because all converge on the true value.
- H_C (correlated hallucination): there is a latent confounder Z (shared corpus, shared teacher model, shared prompt template, shared retrieval index version, shared fine-tune lineage, same bug) such that y_i = g_Z(x) + η_i, where g_Z(x) ≠ f*(x) with probability q (the confounder's hallucination rate). Conditional on Z, errors are independent across i, but marginal error correlation ρ > 0.

Key measurable quantity: pairwise error correlation ρ = P(y_i wrong ∧ y_j wrong) − p², or more precisely the phi coefficient between error indicators.

Under H_T with independent errors at rate p: P(all N agree on same answer | correct) etc. Under H_C: agreement probability inflated.

But we can't observe ground truth directly (that's why we need consensus). So the signals must be computable without labels. That's the crux: detect correlation of *errors* without knowing which are errors. Signals must come from:

(a) Provenance metadata (the verkle tree): lineage overlap, shared ancestors, shared data versions, shared seeds, shared prompts, shared tool versions, timestamp clustering, IP/host clustering.
(b) Output-conditional signals: entropy of the answer distribution, self-consistency under perturbation, calibration signals, token-level logprob patterns, mutual information between outputs beyond what truth induces.
(c) Stress-test signals: inject controlled perturbations (canary questions with known answers), measure joint error rates to estimate ρ empirically per provenance-cluster pair.

## 2. The measured signals

Define for a batch of N responses to query x:

Signal S1 — Provenance overlap (from the Verkle tree). Each response i has provenance vector π_i = (model_id, model_ckpt_hash, prompt_template_hash, retrieval_index_version, tool_versions, sampling_seed, host_id, training_data_merkle_root(s), fine-tune_lineage). Store commitments in a Verkle tree so any subset can be opened with O(log n) witnesses and verified against the root. Measured signal: weighted Jaccard similarity

J_ij = Σ_k w_k 1[π_i[k] = π_j[k]] / Σ_k w_k 1[π_i[k] ∨ π_j[k]]

with weights w_k tuned to empirical correlation contribution (see estimation below). Aggregate: max-pair or mean-top-k J̄ = mean of top-K pairwise J.

Signal S2 — Pairwise error-correlation estimate via canary calibration. Maintain a rolling set of canary queries with known ground truth, routed through the same pipeline components. For each pair of agents (i,j), measure the observed joint error rate on canaries: ĉ_ij = P̂(both wrong). Then

ρ̂_ij = ĉ_ij − p̂_i p̂_j, normalized: φ̂_ij = (ĉ_ij − p̂_i p̂_j)/√(p̂_i(1−p̂_i)p̂_j(1−p̂_j))

This is a direct measurement of the confounding, not a guess. Wilson/Clopper-Pearson intervals give uncertainty. Minimum canary count n_c for resolution: need n_c ≥ z²/(4δ²) roughly to resolve ρ at granularity δ; e.g., δ=0.02, z=2 → n_c ≈ 2500 per pair-cell (or share canaries across pairs since canaries are common).

Actually better: use a shared canary stream; each agent answers all canaries; then per-pair counts come from the same N_c canaries. Standard error of φ̂ ~ sqrt((1−φ²)/N_c)-ish; more precisely delta method: Var(φ̂) ≈ (1/N)[(1+φ²)(p_i+p_j... )]. Keep it simple: report SE ≈ sqrt((1−φ̂²)²/N_c · κ) with κ from the 2×2 table; or just use Fisher's exact / bootstrap. For closed-form rule, use SE formula: SE(φ̂) = sqrt( ((1−φ̂²)^2) / N_c ) as first-order approximation (this is the asymptotic SE of a correlation under bivariate normality; for binary it's approximate but serviceable; better to give exact delta-method).

Exact delta method for phi coefficient from a 2×2 table with cell probabilities: Let a=P(11), b=P(10), c=P(01), d=P(00). φ=(ad−bc)/√((a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d)). Delta method variance is messy; I'll present the standard result: Var(φ̂) ≈ (1/n)[1 − φ²]² adjusted... Actually for tetrachoric it's different. Let me just define the decision rule on ρ̂ = ĉ − p̂_ip̂_j with its exact binomial-based CI, and separately on φ̂ with bootstrap-free conservative bound: SE(ρ̂) ≤ sqrt(p̂_i p̂_j (1−p̂_i)(1−p̂_j)/N_c) + sqrt(p̂_i p̂_j (1−p̂_i)(1−p̂_j))/N_c ... hmm, actually Var(ĉ) = c(1−c)/N_c exactly (binomial if canary outcomes iid within pair). And p̂'s have their own variances but they're estimated from the same canaries — covariance terms. To keep it clean and honest: estimate p̂_i, p̂_j, ĉ_ij from disjoint canary splits, then Var(ρ̂) = c(1−c)/N_{c,1} + p_ip_j(1−p_ip_j)... no wait, Var(p̂_i p̂_j) needs covariances. If splits are disjoint: Var(ρ̂) = c(1−c)/N₁ + [p_j² p_i(1−p_i) + p_i² p_j(1−p_j)]/N₂. That's clean and exact to second order. Good — specify disjoint split.

Signal S3 — Answer-distribution shape. Under H_T with independent noise, conditional on the true answer being one of M candidates, votes follow multinomial with concentration around truth; the number of distinct answers K and the top-share s = max_a n_a/N have known distributions. Under H_C, the distribution collapses onto the confounder's answer even when wrong, OR shows a characteristic bimodality (confounder cluster vs independent cluster). Measured: top-share s, distinct-count K, and the "second-tier mass" m₂ = 1 − s − (mass on known-correct reference if available).

Closed form under H_T (independent, per-agent accuracy p on this query type): P(top-share ≥ s₀) computable via multinomial/Poisson-binomial. Under H_C with fraction α of agents sharing confounder Z: the confounded block votes together with prob (1−q) for the wrong answer g_Z(x); effective sample size drops from N to N_eff = N/(1+(αN−1)ρ̃) where ρ̃ is intra-block correlation. This gives the design-effect formula: N_eff = N / DEFF, DEFF = 1 + (m−1)ρICC with m = average cluster size. This is the classic ICC/design effect from survey statistics — perfect grounding.

So Signal S3 becomes: estimated effective sample size N_eff = N / (1 + (m̄−1)·ICĈ), where ICĈ comes from canary-measured intra-provenance-cluster correlation. Then the decision rule uses N_eff instead of N in the binomial tail.

Signal S4 — Perturbation-stability coupling. Correlated hallucinations are typically coupled to specific surface features of the prompt (shared retrieval snippet, shared misparse). Measure: for each agent, generate T perturbed variants of x (paraphrase, distractor insertion, format change). Compute per-agent flip rate f_i and cross-agent co-flip rate. Under H_T, flips are independent across agents given difficulty; under H_C, co-flips spike when the perturbation breaks the shared confounder. Measured statistic: co-flip lift L = P(flip_i ∧ flip_j) / (f_i f_j) on matched perturbation pairs. L ≈ 1 under independence; L >> 1 indicates shared brittle dependency. Closed form: test statistic Λ = Σ over perturbation pairs of indicator(co-flip), Poisson-binomial under H_T with rate λ₀ = f̄²; reject when Λ exceeds quantile. Or continuous: L̂ with CI via delta method.

Signal S5 — Logprob/token-level fingerprint divergence. Correlated models produce suspiciously aligned error modes: measure edit-distance-normalized disagreement among the *wrong* answers. Under H_T, wrong answers scatter (high conditional entropy H(Y|wrong)); under H_C, wrong answers concentrate (low H(Y|wrong)) because they inherit the same generation path. Measured: conditional entropy Ĥ_wrong = −Σ_a p̂(a|wrong) log p̂(a|wrong), compared to its null value under uniform-over-wrong-space or under fitted independent-error model. Also: normalized compression distance or BLEU/ROUGE-L among wrong-answer strings; high pairwise similarity among wrongs = shared mechanism.

Hmm, but careful: under H_T with low p, most "wrongs" might be the single most plausible distractor too. Need null model: fit independent-error model with per-agent confusion matrices estimated on canaries (per-agent confusion matrix C_i[a_true][a_pred]), predict expected wrong-answer distribution under independence: p_null(a) ∝ Σ_t P(t) Π_i C_i[t][a]-ish... For the aggregate vote vector: under independence, P(vote profile) = Π_i C_i[τ][y_i] marginalized over τ. The sufficient statistic: log-likelihood ratio between "independence model" and "one-latent-confounder model" — this is exactly a latent-class model comparison. That's the principled core!

## 3. The principled core: latent class model LLR

This is the right formal frame. N raters, M possible answers, unknown truth τ ∈ M. 

Model A (H_T): conditional independence given τ. Parameters: per-agent confusion matrices C_i (estimated on canaries — measured, not guessed).
Model B (H_C): mixture: with prob β, all agents in provenance-connected component share latent state Z that determines their answer distribution D_Z (a corrupted distribution concentrated on wrong answer); else independent.

Then compute marginal likelihood under each and take LLR. But closed-form decision rule requested — so reduce to a sufficient statistic with closed-form threshold.

Simplification that keeps it closed-form: decompose by provenance clusters. Partition agents into clusters G_1..G_K by provenance linkage (threshold on J_ij). Within cluster, agents share confounder risk; across clusters, treat as independent after conditioning. Then:

- Between-cluster agreement is evidence for truth (clusters are independent by construction, assuming provenance graph captures dependence channels).
- Within-cluster agreement is discounted by design effect.

Decision rule sketch: Weighted vote with weights = inverse design effect; accept consensus iff weighted top-share exceeds threshold derived from binomial tail with N_eff, AND residual cross-cluster correlation φ̂_cross < threshold.

This is concrete and grounded: it's exactly how survey methodology handles clustered samples (design effects, ICC) and how inter-rater reliability handles correlated raters.

## 4. The closed-form decision rule

Now assemble. Define:

Inputs per query x:
- N responses y_1..y_N with provenance vectors π_i committed in Verkle tree (root R, openings verified at gate).
- Canary-calibrated per-agent accuracy p̂_i and pairwise phi φ̂_ij (with SEs) from rolling canary stream (disjoint-split estimators).
- Provenance similarity matrix J_ij.
- Vote counts n_a over answer space M (top answer â with share s = n_â/N).
- Optional: perturbation co-flip lift L̂, wrong-answer conditional entropy.

Step 1 — Dependence graph construction: edge (i,j) iff J_ij ≥ θ_J OR φ̂_ij ≥ z_φ·SE(φ̂_ij) (i.e., statistically significant positive error correlation). Take connected components = clusters G_1..G_K, sizes m_1..m_K. (Union of metadata-similarity and behaviorally-measured correlation — both measured.)

Step 2 — Effective sample size: ICĈ = pooled within-cluster pairwise phi: ICĈ = Σ_{clusters} Σ_{pairs∈cluster} φ̂_pair / Σ_clusters C(m_k,2). Design effect DEFF = 1 + (m̄ − 1)·ICĈ with m̄ = Σm_k²/N (standard cluster-survey formula, exact for equal-size, standard approx otherwise). N_eff = N/DEFF.

Step 3 — Cross-cluster independence check: compute φ̂_cross over all cross-cluster pairs; require max standardized value below gate: max_{i∈G_a,j∈G_b} φ̂_ij/SE(φ̂_ij) ≤ z_max (else merge clusters and recompute — iterate until stable; fixed-point converges since merging only increases within-cluster mass; cap iterations).

Step 4 — Consensus strength under corrected independence: Under H_T with per-agent accuracies p̂_i and true answer â, the top-vote share satisfies: n_â ~ Poisson-Binomial(N_eff-ish). Cleaner: use weighted score W = Σ_{i: y_i=â} w_i with w_i = 1/(1 + Σ_{j≠i, j~i} φ̂_ij) (down-weight agents embedded in correlated blocks; equivalently w_i = 1/DEFF_i where DEFF_i = 1 + (m_{c(i)}−1)ICĈ). Accept iff

W ≥ w* = q_{1−α} of Poisson-Binomial(Σw_i·p̄) ... hmm, need care: the null for "agreement is illusory" is that agreement arises without truth. Let me define the decision properly as a hypothesis test:

H0 (no reliable truth signal): votes are exchangeable draws from the empirical answer distribution (i.e., agreement level explainable by chance/copying alone, no anchoring to truth).
H1: anchored to truth with per-agent accuracy p̂_i.

Test statistic: T = Σ_i w_i·1[y_i = â]. Under H0 with copying-adjusted null: the null distribution of T given the observed agreement structure... Simpler and defensible: two-sided structure —

Rule: ACCEPT consensus iff ALL of:
(A1) s_adj := W / Σ_i w_i ≥ γ₁, where γ₁ solves the Poisson-Binomial tail: P(PB(w_i p̂_i) ≥ W) ≤ α₁ under the null that each agent independently hits â with its canary-calibrated rate p̂_i — wait, that's not a null, that's assuming truth. Let me think again.

The real question: is the observed agreement more consistent with "all converged on truth" than with "shared artifact"? Both hypotheses predict high agreement! So raw agreement level cannot discriminate — this is the key insight the problem hinges on. Discriminating power must come from signals that differ between the hypotheses:

- Under H_T: wrong-agents' answers scatter according to independent confusion matrices; provenance diversity is irrelevant; perturbation flips uncorrelated; canary φ ≈ 0.
- Under H_C: wrong-agents' answers concentrate on the artifact; provenance overlap high; co-flip lift high; canary φ > 0.

So the closed-form rule should be a likelihood-ratio-style combination of these measured discriminants, with thresholds set for target FPR. Let me define the final statistic as a sum of standardized measured signals (each individually calibrated), combined with weights from measured discriminative power (e.g., each signal's measured AUC or its KL divergence between canary-labeled classes). That yields a closed-form linear score with exact threshold for Gaussianized signals.

Concretely:

z-scored discriminants (each measured on labeled canary events where ground truth known, giving empirical mean μ₀,σ₀ under "artifact-driven agreement" and μ₁,σ₁ under "true convergence" — wait, better: calibrate under H0 = correlated-hallucination regime induced synthetically? Hmm. Ground truth for calibration: canary events where we KNOW the correct answer; run the full fleet; label each canary-batch outcome as "true consensus" (majority correct & would-be accepted) vs "correlated hallucination" (majority wrong due to measured shared component). Since canaries have known answers, these labels are measured, not guessed. From these labeled events, estimate per-signal class-conditional means/variances. Then the decision rule is a quadratic discriminant or, after variance-stabilizing transforms, linear:

D = Σ_k λ_k (S_k − μ_{0k})/σ_{0k} with threshold τ chosen s.t. P(D>τ|H0)=α. With Gaussianization (rank-based inverse-normal transform per signal, calibrated on canary events), the sum under H0 is approximately N(0, Σλ²) if signals decorrelated; whiten: D = λᵀΣ₀⁻¹(S−μ₀), threshold τ = Φ⁻¹(1−α)·sqrt(λᵀΣ₀⁻¹λ)... For closed form, use whitened linear discriminant: D(S) = (μ₁−μ₀)ᵀΣ₀⁻¹S (Fisher LDA direction), classify H1 iff (μ₁−μ₀)ᵀΣ₀⁻¹(S − (μ₀+μ₁)/2) > log(π₀/π₁) + ½log(|Σ₁|/|Σ₀|) — that's exact closed form for Gaussians (QDA/LDA). Give the LDA closed form with measured μ, Σ from canary-labeled events. That is fully "measured-not-guessed": every parameter is an empirical moment from labeled canary events; the rule is the closed-form Bayes rule under Gaussian class-conditionals (justified by CLT over many canary events + inverse-normal transform).

But also the user asked specifically "in the verkle chain / provenance gate" — so integrate: the signals S include provenance-tree-derived features (J stats, lineage entropy, timestamp deltas, witness-failure flags), and the gate enforces: no admission unless (a) all provenance openings verify against root R (cryptographic precondition), (b) D(S) > τ. Also mention hard gates: identical-output-with-distinct-seed detection (copying), seed collision, replay detection via nonce inclusion in the leaf preimage.

Also worth including: the cryptographic angle — Verkle tree specifics: vector commitment with KZG-style polynomial commitments; opening a leaf requires O(1) witnesses (that's the point of Verkle vs Merkle). Provenance leaves: leaf_i = H(nonce_i ‖ y_i ‖ π_i ‖ t_i). Gate verifies openings for the subset used in the decision — so the decision itself is auditable/reproducible on-chain. The decision rule inputs are committed; anyone can recompute D from openings. Deterministic rule ⇒ consensus-on-consensus-audit.

Now let me nail down the exact signal list with formulas, then the exact decision rule, then thresholds/calibration numbers, then failure modes.

### Signals (final list, each with estimator)

S1 — Provenance overlap J̄: weighted Jaccard over π fields; fields: model_family, ckpt_hash, data_roots (set), prompt_template_hash, retriever_version, index_snapshot, sampler_seed, decode_params, host/AS, code_version. Weights w_f learned from canary regression of φ on field-match indicators (measured weights: w_f = E[φ | match_f] from canary pairs — or ridge coefficients). Aggregate A = mean of top decile of pairwise J, or graph density.

S2 — Behavioral error correlation φ̂_ij: from canary stream, disjoint splits: 
p̂_i = e_i/N₁ (e_i = errors on split 1)
ĉ_ij = c_ij/N₂ (co-errors on split 2)
ρ̂_ij = ĉ_ij − p̂_i p̂_j
φ̂_ij = ρ̂_ij / sqrt(p̂_i(1−p̂_i) p̂_j(1−p̂_j))
Var(ρ̂_ij) = ĉ(1−ĉ)/N₂ + p̂_j² p̂_i(1−p̂_i)/N₁ + p̂_i² p̂_j(1−p̂_j)/N₁ (disjoint splits ⇒ independent terms; second-order exact ignoring covariance of products — actually with disjoint splits, p̂_i ⊥ ĉ, p̂_j ⊥ ĉ, and p̂_i ⊥ p̂_j (same split 1 though!). Hmm: p̂_i and p̂_j from same split 1 are correlated through shared canary difficulty. Cov(p̂_i,p̂_j) = Cov(e_i,e_j)/N₁² = (c^{(1)}_ij − p_i p_j)/N₁ where c^{(1)} is co-error count on split 1. So Var(p̂_ip̂_j) includes that covariance term. To keep closed form clean: use triple split or just include the term: Var(ρ̂) = ĉ(1−ĉ)/N₂ + p̂_j²V_i + p̂_i²V_j + 2p̂_ip̂_j·Cov_ij, with V_i = p̂_i(1−p̂_i)/N₁, Cov_ij = (ĉ^{(1)}_ij − p̂_ip̂_j)/N₁. Fine — give this exact expression. Good, that's rigorous.

S3 — Clustered design effect: clusters from union graph (J ≥ θ_J or φ̂ significant at z ≥ 3). ICĈ = pooled within-cluster mean pairwise φ̂. DEFF = 1 + (m̄−1)ICĈ, m̄ = Σm_k²/N. N_eff = N/DEFF. Report N_eff alongside raw N.

S4 — Wrong-answer concentration: conditional entropy of non-plurality answers, and pairwise string similarity among wrong answers (normalized Levenshtein or token-Jaccard), compared against null predicted from per-agent confusion matrices under independence: 
Null prediction: p_null(a) for a ≠ τ: from canary confusion matrices, p_null(a) ∝ Σ_t π_t Π_i C_i(t→a)... simpler operationalization: expected plurality-among-wrong share under independence = max_a Σ_i P(y_i=a, y_i≠τ)/E[#wrong]. Measured deviation Δ_conc = observed wrong-concentration − null. Under H_C, Δ_conc > 0 substantially.

S5 — Perturbation co-flip lift: T paraphrases/perturbations; per agent flip indicator; L̂ = P̂(co-flip)/(f̂_i f̂_j) over matched perturbation sets; significance via Poisson-binomial tail: under independence co-flips ~ PB with rates f̂_if̂_jt; p-value closed form via dynamic program or Chernoff: P(PB ≥ k) ≤ exp(−t k)Π(1+f̂_if̂_j(e^t−1)) minimized over t>0 (Chernoff bound — closed form). Use Chernoff to keep it closed-form: reject independence if min_t [−tk + Σ ln(1+r_l(e^t−1))] < log α.

S6 — Timing/telemetry coherence: inter-response latency correlation, identical-length outputs, identical token-level logprob fingerprints (if exposed), near-duplicate reasoning traces (minhash Jaccard on CoT shingles > θ_dup with distinct declared seeds ⇒ copying flag). Copying is the degenerate case of correlation: hard veto.

S7 — Calibration divergence: per-agent stated confidence vs canary-measured accuracy; correlated hallucination often ships with coherent overconfidence (shared miscalibration). Measured: ECE_i from canaries; signal = variance of ECE within cluster vs across. Weak signal; optional.

Keep the main rule on S1–S5 (+S6 as veto). 

### The closed-form decision rule

Phase 0 (cryptographic gate): verify Verkle openings for all N leaves against published root R; check nonce uniqueness, timestamps within window, no duplicate (y_i, seed) pairs. Fail ⇒ reject before scoring.

Phase 1 (graph): edges E = {(i,j): J_ij ≥ θ_J} ∪ {(i,j): φ̂_ij − 2·SE(φ̂_ij) > 0} (one-sided 97.5% lower bound positive). Components ⇒ clusters.

Phase 2 (veto): if any pair has dup-trace similarity > θ_dup with distinct seeds, or seed collision, or identical byte-output with distinct sampling params ⇒ verdict CORRELATED (copying), no further scoring.

Phase 3 (score): feature vector S = (A, φ̄_within, Δ_conc, log L̂, N_eff/N, ...) — pick 5 features:
x₁ = mean top-decile provenance J
x₂ = ICĈ (pooled within-cluster φ)
x₃ = wrong-answer concentration excess Δ_conc
x₄ = log co-flip lift (Chernoff-significant ones; else 0)
x₅ = 1 − N_eff/N (fraction of effective sample lost to correlation)

Calibration: on labeled canary events (known-τ batches classified: TRUE-CONSENSUS if plurality = τ and accepted; CORR-HALLUC if plurality ≠ τ — note: this labeling is legitimate because canary τ is known by construction), compute class means μ₀,μ₁ and pooled covariance Σ (LDA) or per-class Σ₀,Σ₁ (QDA). Rule (QDA, exact closed form):

Decide H₁ (true consensus) iff
½log(|Σ₀|/|Σ₁|) − ½(S−μ₁)ᵀΣ₁⁻¹(S−μ₁) + ½(S−μ₀)ᵀΣ₀⁻¹(S−μ₀) + log(π₁/π₀) > 0

That IS the closed-form decision rule (Bayes-optimal under Gaussian class-conditionals). With regularized shrinkage covariance Σ_cl = (1−λ)Σ̂ + λ(tr(Σ̂)/d)I to guarantee invertibility.

Threshold operating point: choose posterior cutoff to hit target FPR α*: sweep on held-out canary events; equivalently adjust prior odds log(π₁/π₀) += logit offset. Because everything is measured on canaries, the ROC is measured, not assumed.

Also give the simple interpretable special case (when you don't want QDA): the "corrected quorum" rule:

ACCEPT iff (i) cross-cluster max standardized φ ≤ 3, (ii) no veto, (iii) weighted plurality margin: W = Σ_{i:y_i=â} 1/DEFF_i ≥ q*, where q* is the smallest integer solving the Poisson-Binomial tail P(PB(r_i = p̂_i/DEFF_i) ≥ W) ≤ α under the null of "no truth anchoring" — hmm, again the null issue. Let me define the null correctly for the quorum rule: Null = answers are drawn from the population answer distribution with no common truth, with copying/clustering already accounted by weights. Under this null, P(W ≥ w*) is computable by simulation on canaries... but user wants closed form. Alternative clean formulation: compare likelihood of observed vote vector under (a) independent-confusion model anchored at some τ vs (b) cluster-artifact model. The LLR has closed form given canary-estimated parameters:

LLR(τ) = Σ_i log C_i(τ→y_i) + Σ_{clusters k} log B_k − Σ_i log M_i(y_i), where B_k = mixture weight/artifact distribution term... Getting heavy. 

Better: present BOTH: (1) the exact closed-form QDA rule as the primary gate (fully specified, all parameters measured), and (2) the transparent analytic special case: the design-effect-corrected binomial test with explicit formula:

Under H_T, given true answer = â, per-agent correct probs p̂_i, the number of correct votes K ~ PoissonBinomial(p̂_1..p̂_N). Under H_C with cluster structure, replace p̂_i by effective contributions and N by N_eff: the discriminating testable consequence is that under H_C, agreement does NOT track canary-measured accuracy: regress per-event top-share on Σp̂_i; slope β̂ ≈ 1 under H_T, β̂ ≈ DEFF⁻¹-ish under H_C. Hmm, that's a population-level test, not per-query.

Per-query discrimination fundamentally rests on: provenance overlap, behavioral correlation (canary φ), wrong-scatter shape, co-flip coupling. Agreement level alone is uninformative — say this explicitly, it's the crux insight: "agreement is not evidence; only agreement-that-survives-independence-accounting is."

Let me also handle the "verkle" part concretely: why Verkle not Merkle: N provenance leaves, decision uses subsets (cluster representatives, cross-cluster pairs); Verkle gives O(log N)-size... actually Verkle gives O(1) witness per opening (single proof of ~32–48 group elements regardless of depth) enabling cheap on-chain verification of the exact provenance fields used by D. Commit scheme: root R = VC({leaf_i}); leaf_i commits to (nonce, y_i hash, π_i fields, t_i, agent pubkey). Gate contract verifies openings for: all N leaves (for vote tally), plus the canary-derived parameter commitment (parameters P = (p̂, φ̂ matrix digest) committed in a separate tree updated per epoch). Decision reproducibility: D is pure function of (votes, openings, P-commitments); emit D and its inputs' hashes on-chain ⇒ auditable consensus-about-consensus.

Numbers/thresholds to make it concrete (grounded defaults with rationale):
- θ_J = 0.35 on weighted Jaccard (calibrate: choose θ_J s.t. canary pairs with φ̂ > 0.1 have recall 95% as edges — measured ROC for the edge predictor).
